options.A: Colombia, Peru, Uruguay, and Costa Rica.
options.B: Bhutan, Niger, Cambodia, and Costa Rica.

questions.stem_text: In 2018, about how many chickens were killed for meat production?
questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer of 69 billion reflects the staggering scale of global poultry production in 2018, where chickens accounted for the majority of meat consumption worldwide, underscoring their significance in agricultural economics and food supply chains.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following is true about the global growth rate?

options.A: The global growth rate was four times as high 50 years ago as it is in 2020.
options.B: The global growth rate was two times as high 50 years ago as it is in 2020.
options.C: The global growth rate is two times as high as it is in 2020.
options.D: The global growth rate is four times as high today as it is in 2020.

questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer is based on historical demographic data, which shows that the global growth rate in the 1970s was significantly higher, approximately 2.2% per year, compared to around 1.0% in 2020, highlighting a substantial decline in growth over the past five decades.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following countries emitted the most CO 2 per capita in 2017?
questions.answer_explanation: Canada had one of the highest per capita CO2 emissions in 2017 due to its reliance on fossil fuels for energy production, extensive industrial activities, and a low population density that results in higher emissions per person compared to many other countries.
